answers.stem_only: Relational, transactional data with many relationships and multi-table joins, existing PostgreSQL SQL and tools, fully managed: a managed PostgreSQL-compatible relational database, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (or RDS for PostgreSQL). Not a key-value store, a cache or an S3 query layer.

Heterogeneous Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL migration: use AWS SCT to convert the schema and the PL/SQL code to PL/pgSQL, then AWS DMS for the full load plus ongoing replication (CDC) over the private connection so the final cutover fits the short window. Babelfish is for SQL Server T-SQL, not Oracle PL/SQL, and Aurora read replicas cannot be created from an Oracle source.

Unplanned Regional outage of the primary with data loss accepted: run a managed failover (failover with allow-data-loss) of the Aurora global database to the us-west-2 secondary; the global writer endpoint follows the new primary, so applications keep their connection settings. A switchover needs a healthy primary, and detach-and-repoint or snapshot restore needs connection changes and more work.

Planned move of the primary role with both Regions healthy and no data loss: run a switchover (formerly managed planned failover) of the Aurora global database to us-west-2; it synchronizes the secondary before promoting it, and the global writer endpoint follows the new primary so connection settings stay the same.

Key-value access by session ID, no joins, durable storage required, spiky traffic up to millions of requests, least operational overhead: Amazon DynamoDB (on-demand capacity) with session ID as partition key. A cache alone is not the durable system of record; a relational Aurora cluster adds overhead and does not fit the access pattern or the scale as well.
